correctness.rationale: The LT and Golosov indices reduce exactly to N²/Σx_i² and Σ x_i N/(x_iN+x1²−x_i²) on positive integer profiles. Independently enumerated partitions in weakly decreasing order for each N=2,...,10, grouped by exact (k,x1), and compared both formulas as fractions: no weak-order disagreement through N=9; at N=10 exactly one comparable pair reverses, (4,4,2) vs (4,3,3). Computed LT values 25/9<50/17 and Golosov 21/8>97/37 with exact difference 1/296; common count scaling preserves shares. Complete finite exhaustion rather than isolated numerics proves least N and uniqueness under the stated controls.

evidence: The original articles define the two rational functions of vote shares and discuss differing descriptive behavior; they are cited and credited.
The accessible primary Golosov abstract does not state the sharp first common integer resolution or unique N=10 controlled pair.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The formulas alone are sufficient data for a new finite exhaustive classification but do not automatically determine its least N or uniqueness; the finite census is separately established using every partition up to 10.

value.rationale: Controlling common integer size, represented-party count and leading-party share isolates a mathematically meaningful ordinal distinction between two well-used fragmentation functionals. The exact minimum ten-unit resolution and unique optimizer pair form a natural complete finite classification, not an arbitrary table entry, even though the numerical Golosov gap is small. It does not claim that real electoral datasets typically have ten votes or that either index is preferable.

scientific_limitations: Positive integer partitions only, parties unlabelled and sorted, common N,k,x1; no claims for unconstrained shares or varying leaders.
Full closest Golosov article not accessible, so exact priority risk remains.
